suppliers.exact_statement: Let a P-graded module have support in a finite union of cones lambda_j-Q_+. Choose a finite-rank direct coordinate summand X_f of the free group P containing all lambda_j and alpha_i. Set Y_aux=(⊕_i Z H_i)⊕Hom(X_f,Z), X_aux=Hom(Y_aux,Z), j(x)(H_i)=<x,h_i> and j(x)(f)=f(x), and alpha_i_aux=j(alpha_i). Conversely all original K_h actions are reconstructed from the original label x as q^{<x,h>}; this gives an equivalence between the specified support-graded categories. The construction applies simultaneously to Verma/highest modules and finite tensor products by choosing X_f to contain the participating upper weights and all roots. The auxiliary rational Cartan space decomposes H_min⊕Z, with H_min a finite minimal realization and Z central (all alpha_i vanish on it).

suppliers.exact_statement:
Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half with its skew derivations $e_i',e_i'':U_q^-\to U_q^-$ ([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), fix $i\in I$, and write $f_i^{(n)}=F_i^n/[n]_i!$ for the divided powers ([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]). Then:

(i) $e_i'$ is locally nilpotent on $U_q^-$, and the endomorphism $$P_i:=\sum_{m\ge0}(-1)^m q_i^{-m(m-1)/2}F_i^{(m)}e_i'^{\,m}\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb Q(q)}(U_q^-)$$ is well defined (each sum is finite on each element) and is the projection onto $\operatorname{Ker} e_i'$ along $f_iU_q^-$. In particular $e_i'P_i=0$, $P_iF_i=0$, $P_i^2=P_i$, $P_iu=u$ for $u\in\operatorname{Ker} e_i'$, and $$U_q^-=\operatorname{Ker} e_i'\oplus f_iU_q^-.$$

(ii) Every $u\in U_q^-$ has a unique $i$-string decomposition $$u=\sum_{n\ge0}f_i^{(n)}u_n,\qquad u_n\in\operatorname{Ker} e_i',\qquad u_n=0\ \text{for }n\gg0,$$ and the components are given by $u_n=q_i^{n(n-1)/2}P_ie_i'^{\,n}u$.

(iii) The **Kashiwara operators on the negative half**, defined on the string decomposition by $$\tilde e_iu:=\sum_{n\ge1}f_i^{(n-1)}u_n,\qquad \tilde f_iu:=\sum_{n\ge0}f_i^{(n+1)}u_n,$$ are $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear endomorphisms of $U_q^-$ with $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\operatorname{id}_{U_q^-}$; $\tilde e_iu=0$ if and only if $u\in\operatorname{Ker} e_i'$; $\tilde f_i$ is injective and $\tilde f_i(1)=F_i$. Both operators preserve the root grading and shift its degree by $\mp\alpha_i$, i.e. $\tilde e_i(U_q^-[-\nu])\subseteq U_q^-[-\nu+\alpha_i]$ and $\tilde f_i(U_q^-[-\nu])\subseteq U_q^-[-\nu-\alpha_i]$.

No choice principle is used. Here e_i'^n denotes the ordinary n-fold power of the derivation, not its divided power. The same projector and every string coefficient preserve the Z[q,q^-1] divided-power lattice, as proved by the integral skew-string supplier; this does not assert that lattice's freeness.
suppliers.consumed_clause: Unique divided left strings and normalized field operators with e-tilde f-tilde=id.

(b) **Operator compatibility modulo $q$.** For every $P\in\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha+\alpha_i}$, $$\tilde f_i(Pv_\lambda)\equiv(\tilde f_iP)v_\lambda\bmod q\mathcal L(\lambda),$$ and for every $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ with $\pi_\lambda(b)\ne0$, $$\tilde e_i\pi_\lambda(b)=\pi_\lambda(\tilde e_ib)\qquad\text{in }\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda).$$ Equivalently $\tilde f_i\pi_\lambda=\pi_\lambda\tilde f_i$ on $\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha+\alpha_i}$, where the left-hand side is computed in $V(\lambda)$.

Let $\lambda,\mu\in P^+$ and let $V(\lambda)=L(\lambda)$, $V(\mu)$, $V(\lambda+\mu)$ be the simple integrable highest weight modules with highest weight vectors $v_\lambda,v_\mu,v_{\lambda+\mu}$ ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]). Equip $V(\lambda)\otimes V(\mu)$ with the $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module structure given by the coproduct $\Delta$ of [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]] ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]).

(i) $v_\lambda\otimes v_\mu$ is a highest weight vector of weight $\lambda+\mu$, and its cyclic submodule $U_q(\mathfrak g)(v_\lambda\otimes v_\mu)$ is isomorphic to $V(\lambda+\mu)$.

(ii) There are unique $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module maps $$\Phi_{\lambda,\mu}:V(\lambda+\mu)\to V(\lambda)\otimes V(\mu),\qquad \Psi_{\lambda,\mu}:V(\lambda)\otimes V(\mu)\to V(\lambda+\mu)$$ with $\Phi_{\lambda,\mu}(v_{\lambda+\mu})=v_\lambda\otimes v_\mu$ and $\Psi_{\lambda,\mu}(v_\lambda\otimes v_\mu)=v_{\lambda+\mu}$; they satisfy $\Psi_{\lambda,\mu}\circ\Phi_{\lambda,\mu}=\operatorname{id}_{V(\lambda+\mu)}$, $\Phi_{\lambda,\mu}$ is injective with image $U_q(\mathfrak g)(v_\lambda\otimes v_\mu)$, $\Psi_{\lambda,\mu}$ is surjective, and $V(\lambda)\otimes V(\mu)=\operatorname{Im}\Phi_{\lambda,\mu}\oplus\ker\Psi_{\lambda,\mu}$.

(iii) Let $(\ ,\ )$ be the contravariant form on $V(\lambda)$ of [[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]] and similarly on $V(\mu)$; define the symmetric bilinear form on $V(\lambda)\otimes V(\mu)$ by $(u_1\otimes u_2,v_1\otimes v_2)=(u_1,v_1)(u_2,v_2)$. Then for all $u,v$ and all $i\in I$, $h\in P^\vee$, $$(q^hu,v)=(u,q^hv),\qquad (E_iu,v)=(u,q_iF_iK_i^{-1}v),\qquad (F_iu,v)=(u,q_i^{-1}K_iE_iv),$$ and the maps of (ii) are adjoint: $(\Psi_{\lambda,\mu}u,v)=(u,\Phi_{\lambda,\mu}v)$ for all $u\in V(\lambda)\otimes V(\mu)$, $v\in V(\lambda+\mu)$. In particular $\Phi_{\lambda,\mu}$ is an isometry onto its image.

(iv) The linear map $S_{\lambda,\mu}:V(\lambda)\otimes V(\mu)\to V(\lambda)$ defined by $$S_{\lambda,\mu}(u\otimes v_\mu)=u\quad(u\in V(\lambda)),\qquad S_{\lambda,\mu}\Bigl(V(\lambda)\otimes\sum_{i\in I}F_iV(\mu)\Bigr)=0$$ is well defined, because $V(\mu)=\mathbb Q(q)v_\mu\oplus\sum_{i\in I}F_iV(\mu)$; it is $U_q^-$-linear for the left multiplication action of $U_q^-$, and $S_{\lambda,\mu}\circ\Phi_{\lambda,\mu}$ is the unique $U_q^-$-linear surjection $V(\lambda+\mu)\to V(\lambda)$ with $v_{\lambda+\mu}\mapsto v_\lambda$. Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $V(\lambda)=L(\lambda)$ be the simple integrable highest weight module with highest weight vector $v_\lambda$ ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]). Let $\mathcal L(\lambda),\mathcal B(\lambda),\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$ be the lattices and bases of [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], let $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ be the Kashiwara operators, let $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$, and let $\Phi_{\lambda,\mu},\Psi_{\lambda,\mu}$ be the tensor maps of [[lem-highest-weight-tensor-maps-and-their-adjunction]]. For $\alpha=\sum_in_i\alpha_i\in Q_+$ write $|\alpha|:=\sum_in_i$ and $Q_+(r):=\{\alpha\in Q_+:\ |\alpha|\le r\}$.

(i) For every integer $r\ge0$ the following interlocking statements are all true.
- A(r): $\tilde e_i\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)$ for all $i\in I$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- B(r): $\tilde e_i\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}\subseteq\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$ for all $i$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- C(r): for all $i$, $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $b\in\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i}$ and $b'\in\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, one has $\tilde f_ib=b'$ if and only if $b=\tilde e_ib'$.
- D(r): for all $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}/q\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$.
- E(r): for all $\lambda,\mu\in P^+$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $\Phi_{\lambda,\mu}\bigl(\mathcal L(\lambda+\mu)_{\lambda+\mu-\alpha}\bigr)\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)\otimes\mathcal L(\mu)$.
- F(r): for all $\lambda,\mu\in P^+$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $\Psi_{\lambda,\mu}\bigl((\mathcal L(\lambda)\otimes\mathcal L(\mu))_{\lambda+\mu-\alpha}\bigr)\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda+\mu)$.
- G(r): $\Psi_{\lambda,\mu}\bigl((\mathcal B(\lambda)\otimes\mathcal B(\mu))_{\lambda+\mu-\alpha}\bigr)\subseteq\mathcal B(\lambda+\mu)\cup\{0\}$ for all $\lambda,\mu$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- H(r): $\tilde e_i\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)$ for all $i$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- I(r): $\tilde e_i\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}\subseteq\mathcal B(\infty)\cup\{0\}$ for all $i$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- J(r): for all $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$ and $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ with $\tilde e_ib\ne0$, one has $b=\tilde f_i\tilde e_ib$.
- K(r): $\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}/q\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ for all $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- L(r): $\pi_\lambda\bigl(\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}\bigr)=\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ for all $\lambda\in P^+$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- M(r): for all $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $i\in I$, $\lambda\in P^+$ and $P\in\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha+\alpha_i}$, one has $\tilde f_i(Pv_\lambda)\equiv(\tilde f_iP)v_\lambda\bmod q\mathcal L(\lambda)$.

Work in the finite-support auxiliary regular datum before choosing fundamental or arbitrarily large dominant weights, then transport the chosen label grading back. Choice is inherited only from the generic/classical component-rank supplier underlying the field negative-half form; choosing a basis in one finite-dimensional weight space and taking its field dual require no further AC. $$\tilde f_i(b_1\otimes b_2)=\begin{cases}\tilde f_ib_1\otimes b_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)>\varepsilon_i(b_2),\\ b_1\otimes\tilde f_ib_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)\le\varepsilon_i(b_2),\end{cases}\qquad \tilde e_i(b_1\otimes b_2)=\begin{cases}\tilde e_ib_1\otimes b_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)\ge\varepsilon_i(b_2),\\ b_1\otimes\tilde e_ib_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)<\varepsilon_i(b_2),\end{cases}$$

No finite dimensionality, bounded support or uniform nilpotence is assumed, and no choice principle is used.

Let $(L,B)$ be a crystal basis of an integrable weight module $M$ in the sense of [[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]], let $i\in I$, $\lambda\in P$ and $u\in L_\lambda$, and let $u=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n)}u_n$ be the admissible $i$-string decomposition of $u$: the sum is finite, $u_n\in\ker E_i\cap M_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}$, and $u_n=0$ whenever $n>\langle h_i,\lambda+n\alpha_i\rangle$ ([[thm-unique-kashiwara-i-string-decomposition]]). Then:

(a) **Components lie in the lattice.** $u_n\in L\cap M_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}$ for every $n$.

(b) **Lattice string decomposition.** $L_\lambda=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\tilde f_i^{\,n}\bigl(L_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}\cap\ker E_i\bigr)$, the sum being direct because admissible decompositions are unique; equivalently $L=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\tilde f_i^{\,n}(L\cap\ker E_i)$.

(c) **Single surviving component.** If $u+qL=0$ in $L_\lambda/qL_\lambda$, then $u_n\in qL$ for every $n$. If $u+qL\in B_\lambda$, then there is exactly one index $n_0$ with $u_{n_0}\notin qL$, and for it $u_{n_0}+qL\in B_{\lambda+n_0\alpha_i}$, $u\equiv F_i^{(n_0)}u_{n_0}\pmod{qL}$ and $u_{n_0}+qL=\tilde e_i^{\,n_0}(u+qL)$; in particular $n_0=\varepsilon_i(u+qL)$ ([[def-crystal-graph-epsilon-phi-and-weight]]), and $\tilde e_iu$ and $\tilde f_iu$ are the residues of $F_i^{(n_0-1)}u_{n_0}$ and $F_i^{(n_0+1)}u_{n_0}$.

Everything is a statement about the fixed lattice $L$ and the operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$; no finite-dimensionality, bounded support, uniform nilpotence or choice principle is assumed. Here F_i^(−1)u is interpreted as0, and F_i^(a+1)u=0 for a top of coroot weight a, so the final formulas include both finite-string endpoints.
